Damn dude, 800 cal/day sounds really, really low. I've been counting calories for about 2 months and noticed between 1200-1600/day was ok, but only for a limited time. After about a week I noticed in the gym my body was losing strength.

To be fair, I'm quite thin and go cycling/surfing/to the gym about 3-5 times a week, so we're not yet playing the same game.

You're doing lots of things right already, and I might advise to slightly increase your intake, and to adopt an active lifestyle. It could be you'll hold on to your schedule much easier and longer.

That I think you can do quite cheaply, although I'm not an expert in your limitations: swimming, cycling, hiking, in the gym (maybe there's a cheap one?)

Everything basically is fine, as long as you start out small and increase the intensity just a tiny bit each time.

Get your BMR and TDEE figured out (tons of calculators online) at stick to eating around your BMR at least. If that sounds confusing then download an app like Lose it (I use it every day to track my food) and it will suggest the number of calories you need to eat to lose 1-2lbs a week which is a go0d steady rate. You need to change your eating habits, not just go on a diet as a temp fix, sustainable change in eating is the key to long term fat loss.

Hello @Whim. Welcome to /v/fatpeoplehelp . I read through everything and understand what's up with you. First off, congratulations on losing 42 pounds so far and good work on looking for help to do things better. You have a bunch of stuff going on, so let me bulletize this...

  1. If you haven't yet, please read through the sticky. I'm sure there are some things I still need to add or modify, but the general information in it is sound. If you can understand what you need to do for yourself then you've achieved the kind of self empowerment that will sustain you through the rest of your life.
  2. It is exceptionally difficult to get the macro/micronutrients your body needs on 800 calories a day for either a man or a woman. The types of foods you eat are definitely the right kinds, but it would be good to track the numbers so you know if you're depleting yourself. Being your size (No shame here. Just pointing to what your body type does.) you can usually float the macronutrients for a while, but it WILL catch up to you. Like Swolemaiden said, you need to figure out what you're Total Daily Energy Expenditure is and focus on eating a calorie level that will let you lose 1-2 pounds a week.
  3. PCOS is a bitch. Fortunately, you can make PCOS work for you if you know how. One of the "neat tricks" with PCOS is the testosterone boost symptom that many people get. Fun fact: Many high level female athletes have PCOS and use the T-boost to their advantage. First off, reducing your fast acting carbs (chocolate, donuts, etc) is critical. This is something you're going to need to stay away from if at all possible. The insulin resistance side is what will get you. Now with that stated, look at more protein. Whatever you're eating in protein you should probably eat more of it. Why? Because you're going to start working out. Right. Now. Your body is going to respond to muscle gain a bit more readily than most women.
  4. Anaerobic exercise: Since you're not close to a gym there are many things you can do, or will be able to do as you lose weight. Bodyweight exercises for your anaerobic exercise is fine. Just as long as you do it and do it often. While you're reading this, highlight this sentence, stand up, do 10 bodyweight squats, sit down, breathe, continue reading. There, you just did some anaerobic exercise and didn't die. Keep doing that sort of thing. Build up to more. Work on trying pushups and other exercises. You don't even have to break a sweat, but you probably will once you start doing more and more. You're going to look great once you lose all the extra weight. Just keep doing "stuff".
  5. Aerobic/cardio: Walk. Walk a lot. This is a totally underrated form of exercise. Because of your current size it can be pretty rough on your body to do high intensity exercise. From doing nothing, Low Intensity, Sustained Stress (LISS) cardio is some pretty good stuff. Plus you're getting sunshine. Plus you're looking around at stuff in your neighborhood, giving your brain some exercise. A walk isn't going to kill you and will probably make you feel better overall. Walking is cardio for people that doing like to do cardio. It's easy and burns more calories than you would think.

You're already doing a great job just by doing "something" about it. Keep that shit up!
Don't lose fat too fast or you'll end up with excess skin. Do a research on how much weight per period of time is ok.
